newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to start regulated short sales of stock.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to start regulated short sales of stock.

text.p: Malaysia's Securities Commission has approved rules on regulated short selling of stock which will be implemented beginning on Sept. 30, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Thursday.
Short-selling is the practice of selling securites that an investor does not own in the expectation of buying them later at lower prices.
Such transactions had been illegal in Malaysia.
In a statement, the KLSE said the Securities Commission approved Rule 22, which include policy objectives stipulated by the market watchdog.

They include: identification of all regulated short sales at the time the order is given to the stockbroking firm, the assurance that the stock seller is able to deliver the securities in the transaction, and the selection of securities in the approved class of only highly liquid, high-capitalisation shares.

In June, the Securities Commission said that short-selling would initially be confined to around 32 of the "bluest of the blue chips" which met a strict criteria of a large public float, heavy monthly share volume and a certain number of shareholders.

Under the Securities Commission policies, only stockbroking companies which have in place approved written guidelines on "Know Your Customers" practices would be permitted to engage in regulated short selling.
Under such practices, investors must be made aware of the risks of short selling and have the capacity to meet financial commitments involved in it.
